root_cause.text: The zynqmp_nvmem driver incorrectly used `sizeof(bytes)` (the size of a size_t pointer/variable) instead of the actual `bytes` value in dma_alloc_coherent and dma_free_coherent calls, and also used `bytes` instead of `sizeof(value)` in memcpy, causing undersized DMA buffer allocation and potential buffer overread during memory copy operations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows three critical fixes: (1) changing `dma_alloc_coherent(dev, sizeof(bytes), ...)` to `dma_alloc_coherent(dev, bytes, ...)` on line 103, (2) changing `dma_free_coherent(dev, sizeof(bytes), ...)` to `dma_free_coherent(dev, bytes, ...)` on line 137, and (3) changing `memcpy(&value, val, bytes)` to `memcpy(&value, val, sizeof(value))` on line 83. The variable `bytes` is a size_t representing the actual buffer size needed, while `sizeof(bytes)` evaluates to typically 8 bytes on 64-bit systems, causing DMA allocation to be drastically undersized. Additionally, the memcpy was copying `bytes` amount of data into a 4-byte `unsigned int value` variable, risking buffer overflow.
